slot.brief: Real vs ideal gas conceptual — under what conditions does a real gas deviate most from ideal behaviour, given the van der Waals constant assumptions — one-line conceptual answer.

stem: According to the van der Waals equation, under which conditions does a real gas show the maximum deviation from ideal gas behaviour?

verdicts.working: At low temperature, intermolecular attractions matter more; at high pressure, finite molecular volume matters more. Both increase deviation from ideal-gas behavior.

working:
Ideal gas behaviour assumes negligible molecular volume and no intermolecular forces. At low temperature, molecules move slowly and attractive forces become significant. At high pressure, molecules are forced close together, so molecular volume and intermolecular interactions become important.

Independent check: At low temperature, intermolecular attractions matter more; at high pressure, finite molecular volume matters more. Both increase deviation from ideal-gas behavior.
solution: Ideal behaviour assumes negligible molecular volume and intermolecular forces. At low temperature, attractions become more significant; at high pressure, finite molecular volume and interactions become important. Thus, deviation is maximum at low temperature and high pressure.
